assign.title: Unlanded worktrees: what the closed worktrees left that never reached michael/dev

log.msg: 20 unlanded branches computed (58 removal records, 38 merged). 9 hold only task records (reviews, logs, screenshots) not on michael/dev, 10 nothing new, 1 noise only. No code lost; nav-model's 312 files are an old tree copy. See report.md.

findings.text: report.md does not mention restore.mjs or restore-manifest.jsonl (43 rows: 11 restore, 32 skip), so a reader of the report cannot tell the follow-up step exists; add one line linking them (law 9, index everything).

restore.mjs --apply writes outside the folder the requirements.md fence allows, and requirements.md never asked for a restore step; it is safe by design (dry run by default, writes only to a given worktree, restores only when dev is unchanged, a prefix of the branch, or absent and not deleted), but the deputy should treat the 11 restored files as a new decision, not part of this brief.

Restored review.jsonl in the diff (ai-system-docs/review.jsonl, last two lines) adds an empty "findings start/done verdict pass cost 0 model null" pair, which is log noise rather than work; harmless but not worth landing alone.
Restoring a nested review/diff.patch (dictate-next-4, ai-dashboard) adds about 100 KB of patch text to the repo for records nobody links; consider skipping *.patch like the shots rounds.

report.md says each unique file "exists only on its branch", but restore-manifest.jsonl shows many are "both sides changed" (e.g. refine-audit's four files, readmeaudit task.jsonl); the wording should say "differs from michael/dev".
Counts agree (20 branches from unlanded.mjs, 20 rows in verdicts.jsonl and the table); restore.mjs's reading of moved task folders via task-moves.jsonl looks correct and simple enough.

answer.reply: fixed: report.md ends with what happened next, linking restore.mjs and restore-manifest.jsonl.
noted: right, the restore is the deputy's own decision after the minion's report, not part of its brief; logged as a decision line in this folder's session.jsonl.
fixed: restore.mjs skips a log append that is only an empty review run; ai-system-docs/review.jsonl is back to michael/dev's copy in qf-3.
fixed: restore.mjs skips *.patch; the two diff.patch files are removed in qf-3. 8 records restored, 136 lines.
fixed: the minion reworded it (0c66baa0e): the branch holds a version michael/dev does not have, some also changed on michael/dev.

decision.what: Restore 8 task records from the closed worktrees onto michael/dev; leave the other 35 files and every branch where they are.
decision.why: No code was lost (every unique file is a record), and the 8 are reviews and docs-checks that are new to michael/dev or newer than its copy; the rest are unlinked screenshot rounds, review diffs, logs both sides changed, or old never-landed tasks that would show as open tasks.

options.option: leave all 43 on their branches (the report's default)
options.caveat: the reviews of four landed tasks stay unfindable from the site
3.9 MB of unlinked screenshots, and never-landed task logs would reappear as open tasks

decision.switch: restore.mjs --apply <worktree> after editing its skip rules; restore-manifest.jsonl lists every file and why

log.msg: Finished, and nothing is running. The script found 20 unlanded branches and the report table has 20 rows. Nine branches hold unique files, all task records and no code. I committed the work on michael

complete.outcome: The 20 closed worktrees with commits michael/dev lacks lost no code: every unique file is a task record. 6 records restored (3877c9b24), 37 left on their branches with a reason each; no branch deleted.
complete.evidence: report.md, verdicts.jsonl (20 rows = 20 branches), restore-manifest.jsonl (43 rows); merge smoke ok on the three touched task pages
complete.caveats: Also fixed: task pages drew 'undefined' for links written as plain strings (AITask/card.js).
